question.problem: Given that $(x+3)$ and $(x-1)$ are factors of $f(x)=a{x}^{3}+7{x}^{2}+bx-9,$ then $a+b=$
question.worked_solution:
According to the factor theorem, if $(x-r)$ is a factor of $f(x),$ then the root $x=r$ is also a root of $f(x).$ 

Here, we are considering the factors $(x+3)$ and $(x-1).$ The roots of these factors can be found by setting the factors equal to $0$ and solving:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+3=0 & \,⇒\,x=-3 \\ x-1=0 & \,⇒\,x=1\end{aligned}
$$

According to the factor theorem, then, since $(x+3)$ and $(x-1)$ are factors of $f(x),$ the roots $x=-3$ and $x=1$ are also roots of $f(x).$ This means $f(-3)=0$ and $f(1)=0,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-3) & =0 \\ a(-3)^{3}+7(-3)^{2}+b(-3)-9 & =0 \\ -27a-3b+63-9 & =0 \\ -27a-3b & =-54 \\ -9a-b & =-18, \\  \\ f(1) & =0 \\ a(1)^{3}+7(1)^{2}+b(1)-9 & =0 \\ a+b+7-9 & =0 \\ a+b & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

This gives a system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-9a-b=-18 \\ a+b=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the equations, we eliminate $b$ and get

$$
-8a=-16\,⇒\,a=2.
$$

Substituting $a=2$ in either equation gives $b=0.$ So our solutions are $a=2$ and $b=0.$ Finally then,

$$
a+b=2+0=2.
$$
